title: Vulcan calibrated plates review (the cheapest option out there)
summary: Reviews the Vulcan calibrated kilo plates after about seven months in his home gym. He recommends them as the cheapest branded calibrated plates, valuing exact weight for balanced loading, but notes the paint chips and rubs off, the plates are slippery, and the bundles skew toward 25 kg plates with too few small plates.

claims.claim: He bought Vulcan calibrated plates for his home gym about seven months before the review.
Vulcan plates are among the cheapest calibrated plates and the cheapest branded option with marked weights; unmarked black cast iron calibrated plates can be cheaper.
He doesn't care much about plates, but wanted exact weight so the bar holds what he loads and both sides are balanced; a several-pound imbalance at heavy loads can be dangerous and throw you off.
The plates have a lip that lets you pinch-grip them, but the paint makes them slippery; dropping them is destructive.
All plates are the same thickness except the 25 kg plate, which is thicker; the 25 kg and 20 kg share the same diameter.
The paint looks good and shiny but chips easily and rubs onto racks when plates bump them, even accounting for his rough handling.

At launch he bought a bundle of 600-700 lbs cheaply, but Vulcan's bundles are mostly 25 kg plates with only a pair of each smaller size, leaving you short on fractional plates and 5 kg plates for dumbbells.
Even the 1.25 kg plates are branded and marked, which he appreciates.
They are iron, not bumper plates: noisy, and you need a platform or sturdy rubber mats because they will break anything else; they slide onto the sleeve well without chipping it.
He recommends Vulcan calibrated plates for a home gym if you want standardised, calibrated plates.
